title: The ten-canonical Hilbert parameter and projective-frame torsors
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and $g\geq2$. Put $d=20(g-1)$, $r=19(g-1)$ and $P(m)=dm+1-g$. Let $Z=\operatorname{Hilb}^{P}(\mathbf P^{r-1}_k)$ be the projective finite-type $k$-scheme $H_P$ of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the identity embedding $E=\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$: it represents flat finitely presented closed families in $\mathbf P^{r-1}$ with fibre Hilbert polynomial $P$. For the curves $C\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}$ described below, this index polynomial is $m\mapsto\chi(C,\mathcal O_C(m))=dm+1-g$. It contains a $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$-invariant locally closed subscheme $J$ representing the following functor: over a $k$-scheme $T$, its points are unpointed stable genus-$g$ curves $f:C\to T$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] together with a projective frame $\mathbf P(f_*\omega_{C/T}^{\otimes10})\simeq\mathbf P^{r-1}_T$, identified up to isomorphism of the framed curve. Here $\omega_{C/T}$ is the relative dualizing invertible module (the relative Serre-duality line), and $\mathbf P(E)$ is the projective bundle of one-dimensional quotients of a finite-rank locally free module $E$. For these families $f_*\omega_{C/T}^{\otimes10}$ is locally free of rank $r$, commutes with every base change, and evaluation gives the closed ten-canonical embedding. The line $\mathcal O_C(1)$ of a framed embedding is only required locally on $T$ to be isomorphic to $\omega_{C/T}^{\otimes10}$; a line pulled back from $T$ is allowed. The sheaf of projective frames of each such family is a Zariski locally trivial $G$-torsor. A $G$-torsor means a scheme locally isomorphic to $G\times T$ with its usual simply transitive action. Forgetting the frame gives an equivalence of groupoids, natural in $T$, between stable genus-$g$ curves over $T$ and pairs consisting of a $G$-torsor $E\to T$ and a $G$-equivariant morphism $E\to J$. These pairs, with equivariant isomorphisms as arrows, define $[J/G]$. Here $G$ is the group scheme of linear automorphisms of $\mathbf A^r$ modulo scalar automorphisms. Projective and finite type are [def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Section 3.3, Definition 9 and the projective-frame discussion, printed pp.15--16; equivalence after forgetting the frame: paragraph after Corollary 11, printed p.17. Local PDF WANTED; author exposition read online. Arbitrary-field projective-frame descent formulation written by agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain $Z=H_P$, projective and finite type, with its universal flat finitely presented closed family $p:\mathcal C\to Z$. The polynomial in this representability statement agrees with $\chi(\mathcal C_z,\mathcal O(m))$ by [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality]. Since $d=20(g-1)>0$, [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension] shows that every geometric fibre has dimension one. Thus the universal family is a family to which the curve-stack open-locus statement applies.

source.place: 0BEM and 0BEV; universal family from the item statement and Hilbert representability

proof.text: Let $U\subset Z$ be the open subscheme where the universal family is stable of genus $g$, using [lem-sfb-stable-and-smooth-family-open-loci]. This has the required universal property on every test scheme, rather than only on geometric points. Over $U$ the line $\omega=\omega_{\mathcal C/U}$ exists and commutes with all base changes by [lem-sfb-gorenstein-curve-relative-dualizing]. Also $p_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal O_U$ universally by [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections], since stable fibres are geometrically reduced and nonempty connected.

For any stable family $f:C\to T$, set $L=\omega_{C/T}^{\otimes10}$. The preceding dualizing construction and [lem-sfb-stable-curve-pluricanonical-linear-series] show on every geometric fibre that $H^q(C_t,L_t)=0$ for $q>0$ and $h^0(C_t,L_t)=19(g-1)=r$. Apply the general form of [sk-thm-picard-perfect] with $i=0$ and this $r$. It gives $V=f_*L$ locally free of rank $r$ and commuting with every base change, on all of $T$. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is proper and finitely presented, and $L$ is finitely presented and flat over $T$ because $f$ is flat and $L$ invertible. No reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ enters.

source.place: 0E8X and 0BS6; perfect-complex degree-zero locus as in sk-thm-picard-perfect

proof.text: The evaluation $f^*V\to L$ is surjective. Indeed its finite-type cokernel has zero reduction at each point of $C$, since base change identifies the fibre map with evaluation of the very ample complete series in [lem-sfb-stable-curve-pluricanonical-linear-series]; [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] then annihilates that cokernel stalk. The quotient property [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] gives $i:C\to\mathbf P_T(V)$ pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $L$. Its geometric fibre maps are closed immersions by the same field lemma.

source.place: 01OA quotient construction; curves.tex 0E8X; local Nakayama argument

proof.text: The map $i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], since its target is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Each fibre of $i$ over a target point is either empty or a single closed point: this follows by taking the geometric fibre over its image in $T$, where $i$ is a closed immersion. Thus $i$ is locally quasi-finite, by [pqf-def-quasifinite], and [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes it finite. On an affine target open its algebra map $A\to B$ has finite cokernel $Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] its reduction over each residue field of $T$ is surjective, since the fibre map is closed. At a target point $y$ over $t$, $Q_y/\mathfrak m_tQ_y=0$; reducing further modulo $\mathfrak m_y$ and applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] gives $Q_y=0$. Hence $A\to B$ is surjective and $i$ is a closed immersion. This proves the relative embedding assertion by an explicit affine cokernel argument.

source.place: 02LS, (3) implies (1), followed by finite-algebra Nakayama; no extra fibrewise-immersion lemma

proof.text: On the universal stable curve over $U$, put $M=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(1)\otimes\omega^{-10}$. Apply [lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed] to this invertible module. Its universal $p_*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ hypothesis was checked in step 2. It gives an immersion $K\to U$ of finite presentation such that a test map $T\to U$ factors through $K$ exactly when $M_T\simeq f_T^*N$ for a finite locally free $N$ on $T$. Here $N$ has rank one: every fibre of $f_T$ is nonempty and the pullback has rank one. Thus $N$ is invertible. Conversely, Zariski local isomorphisms $M_T\simeq\mathcal O$ give a global such $N$: on overlaps their ratios are units on $C$, and these are exactly base units because $f_*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_T$ universally. The ratios satisfy the cocycle condition, so glue $N$. This is precisely the base-line-twist condition, including nilpotent test schemes.

source.place: 0BDP, lemma-diagonal-picard-flat-proper; local trivializations glue the rank-one base module

proof.text: Over $K$, the module $W=p_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(1)$ is locally free of rank $r$ and commutes with arbitrary base change: locally trivialize the base line $N$ of step 6 and use step 3. The coordinate restrictions form a map $\alpha:\mathcal O_K^r\to W$. Let $J\subset K$ be its isomorphism open, given by [lem-sc-finite-locally-free-map-iso-open]; locally it is the open where $\det\alpha$ is a unit. Therefore $J\to Z$ is an immersion (a locally closed subscheme). This open is essential: equality of the hyperplane line with $\omega^{10}$ up to a base twist alone does not force an embedding into $\mathbf P^{r-1}$ to be a complete linear series. The construction of $K$ and this open both commute with arbitrary base change.

source.place: 0BDP followed by the determinant isomorphism open; Morrison Definition 9 with completeness imposed explicitly

proof.text: Given a stable family and a projective frame $\phi:\mathbf P_T(V)\simeq\mathbf P^{r-1}_T$, compose its embedding from step 5 with $\phi$. By [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl], Zariski locally $\phi$ is induced by a matrix, and its hyperplane line differs from $L$ by a line from $T$. On such opens the coordinate restrictions are a basis of $V$, so the resulting Hilbert map factors through $J$. Its fibre polynomial is $20(g-1)m+1-g$ by [lem-sfb-stable-curve-pluricanonical-linear-series], which is its coordinate-ring Hilbert polynomial by [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality]; so [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] puts it in the specified $Z$, not a different Hilbert component.

source.place: 4.2.3 and 4.2.7, composed with the complete linear series; curves.tex 0BS6

proof.text: Conversely a $T$-point of $J$ gives a stable family with $\mathcal O_C(1)\simeq L\otimes f^*N$ and the coordinate isomorphism $\mathcal O_T^r\simeq f_*\mathcal O_C(1)$. Locally trivialize $N$. The latter isomorphism gives a frame of $V=f_*L$, hence a projective frame. Changing the trivialization multiplies that frame by a unit from $T$, so its projectivization is unchanged by [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl]; the projective frames glue. Evaluation recovers the original embedding, so this construction and step 8 are inverse. A different chosen line comparison also differs by a base unit, by universal $f_*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_T$, and gives the same result. This proves the representing property independently of all auxiliary choices.

source.place: 4.1.4 and 4.2.3, inverse construction and scalar ambiguity

proof.text: The two constructions preserve arrows and every base change. An isomorphism of framed families gives the same embedded closed subscheme; conversely equality of subschemes supplies the unique compatible curve isomorphism. There are no residual automorphisms of a framed curve: a compatible automorphism commutes with its closed immersion, hence is the identity, and the completeness isomorphism in step 7 determines the projective frame uniquely. Change of coordinates in $G$ preserves stability, the base-line-twist condition and invertibility of $\alpha$; hence the $G$-action on $Z$ preserves $J$ scheme-theoretically by its universal property. Thus the representing property and $G$-invariance hold over all test schemes, not only over fields.

source.place: 4.2.3 universal quotient property and the Hilbert universal property

proof.text: For a stable $C/T$, apply [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] to $V=f_*\omega^{10}$. Its projective-frame scheme $E$ is a Zariski locally trivial $G$-torsor. The universal frame on $E$ gives $E\to J$ by steps 8--10; changing frame is exactly changing coordinates, so this map is equivariant. A curve isomorphism induces the canonical map on its dualizing line and on $V$, hence an equivariant isomorphism of these pairs.

For the inverse, let $E\to T$ be a $G$-torsor with an equivariant map to $J$. For an fppf torsor, [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] supplies an etale trivializing cover; for a Zariski torsor use its given cover. Pull back the universal stable curves on $J$ to this cover. They are flat proper finitely presented curves with one-dimensional geometric fibres, hence objects of $\mathfrak C$ in [lem-sfb-nodal-curve-stack-smooth]. Torsor transitions give coordinate changes and curve isomorphisms; equivariance gives their cocycle identities. That node explicitly asserts effective etale descent and the etale sheaf property for isomorphisms. Thus the datum descends to an algebraic-space curve over $T$, with uniquely descending compatible arrows. The universal stable-genus-$g$ open of [lem-sfb-stable-and-smooth-family-open-loci] is all of $T$: its pullback to the surjective cover is the whole cover. That statement ensures the descended curve is a scheme with the required projective-bundle projectivity. No descent of $\mathcal O(1)$ as a $G$-linearized line is needed.

source.place: quot.tex Tags 0D52 (lemma-curves-stack), 0D5A (theorem-curves-algebraic); moduli-curves.tex 0E76 and 0E78: effective etale descent followed by the universal stable open

proof.text: On the trivializing cover, steps 8--9 identify the given torsor with the projective-frame torsor of the descended curve. These identifications agree on overlaps: their transitions are exactly the given projective coordinate changes. They glue to an equivariant isomorphism preserving the map to $J$. In particular an initially fppf torsor admitting such a map is Zariski locally trivial. Starting with a stable curve, reconstruction from its local framed embeddings descends its own identity cocycle and recovers that curve. By the explicit etale sheaf property for isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-nodal-curve-stack-smooth], compatible curve isomorphisms glue uniquely; the frame-scheme assertion in [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] does the same for compatible torsor maps. The two constructions are therefore inverse and fully faithful on arrows. After any $T^{\prime}\to T$, the pulled-back cover and all evaluation and transition maps are the same construction for the pullback family; uniqueness of descended isomorphisms gives the natural comparison. This proves the natural equivalence with $[J/G]$.

source.place: quot.tex Tag 0D52 (lemma-curves-stack): sheaf property for isomorphisms, descent uniqueness, and projective-frame transition maps
